relevant_files.relevance: Q1: temp+rename publish. tmpPath = this.dataFilePath + '.tmp' (FIXED, not per-instance/per-pid), bakPath = this.dataFilePath + '.bak'. Sequence: writeFile(tmpPath) -> copyFile(dataFilePath, bakPath) best-effort -> rename(tmpPath, dataFilePath). On failure: logs '[WorkspaceService] Flush failed:', unlinks tmpPath best-effort, then re-throws (line 1749-1753). The doc comment at lines 1710-1715 explicitly names the shared-tmp-path race ('Two flushes running at once share one `.tmp` path, so the first rename moves it away and the second finds no source') but the stated mitigation (flushChain, lines 1712-1721/1730-1735) only serializes writes queued through the SAME WorkspaceService instance (same process) — it is an in-memory promise chain, not a filesystem lock, so it does not protect two separate process instances sharing the checkout.

relevant_files.relevance: Q2: process-level fate of a bootstrap flush error. startServer()'s own try/catch (opened at line 964) is what actually catches an EPERM/rename error thrown from CommandPresetService.initialize()->flushToDisk() (or the other three stores' initialize paths) — NOT the process 'uncaughtException'/'unhandledRejection' handlers at lines 175-190 (setupFatalErrorLogging), since the throw happens on the awaited startServer() call chain, not asynchronously outside it. The catch logs '[Fatal] Failed to start server:' and calls process.exit(1), which is the observed 'kills the dev server' symptom. startServer() is invoked at line 1694: `startServer().then(() => setupGracefulShutdown());` — a rejection here (if it ever escaped the internal catch) would otherwise surface as an unhandled rejection, but as written it does not escape because of the internal catch/process.exit(1).

This raises the collision probability specifically for the 'two processes booting from one checkout' scenario in the intent.

relevant_files.relevance: Q3: the only existing automated test that drives concurrent writes at one of these stores. It creates a SINGLE WorkspaceService instance pointed at a temp dataFile (helper makeService(), lines 34-51) and issues concurrent calls (Promise.allSettled of 8x service.save(true), line 63; interleaved save()/save(true) calls in later tests) against that one instance. Determinism/race technique: uses a large tab list (line 30-33 comment: 'A store large enough that a single write does not finish inside one thread-pool tick... an empty store lets two concurrent writes complete before either rename and hides the defect') to force overlap of the writeFile()/rename() I/O windows, and a debounce-timing trick (`await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 0))`, lines 87/101/109) to land an immediate save inside an in-flight debounced flush. This test suite ONLY exercises the in-process flushChain serialization guard; it does NOT construct two separate service instances (i.e. does not simulate two OS processes) pointed at the same dataFilePath, so it does not cover the cross-process race described in the intent.
Q4: dataPath is configurable per-instance via constructor options.dataPath, defaulting to DEFAULT_DATA_PATH = './data/command-presets.json' (line 18) — a path relative to process.cwd().

relevant_files.signature: commandPresetService = new CommandPresetService(); terminalShortcutService = new TerminalShortcutService(); recoveryOptionService = new RecoveryOptionService(); workspaceService = new WorkspaceService(sessionManager, { recoveryOptionService });
relevant_files.relevance: Q4 (decisive): at the actual bootstrap call sites, NONE of the four constructors receive a dataPath override — all four fall through to their DEFAULT_DATA_PATH, which resolves relative to process.cwd(). Because BuilderGate is normally started from the checkout root, two processes started from the same checkout (or two checkouts sharing the same server/data/ via a symlink/mount) resolve to the identical absolute dataFilePath, which is the structural precondition for the race in the intent. No env var (e.g. no BUILDERGATE_DATA_* found) overrides these four paths; only BUILDERGATE_SERVER_ROOT affects SSLService's cert path (server/src/services/SSLService.ts:20), not these JSON stores.

missing_evidence: No automated test anywhere in server/src or tools/ constructs two separate service instances (or two child processes) pointed at the same on-disk dataFilePath to deterministically reproduce the cross-process EPERM/rename collision described in the intent; WorkspaceServiceFlushConcurrency.test.ts (server/src/services/WorkspaceServiceFlushConcurrency.test.ts:1-141) only covers concurrency within one process/one service instance.

No retry-on-rename, no lock-file (e.g. proper-lockfile, flock, advisory lock, PID lock file), and no cross-process mutex of any kind was found anywhere under server/src or tools/ via grep for 'lock', 'flock', 'retry' near rename/EPERM handling — the only concurrency guard found (flushChain / mutationChain / saveQueue promise chains) is in-process only.

Whether Windows EPERM (vs POSIX EEXIST/ENOENT-style races) is the actually observed failure mode was not verified by test or by any Windows-specific comment beyond the WorkspaceService.ts:1713 doc comment describing the shared-tmp-path failure mechanism in general (rename source disappearing) — no direct citation of an EPERM error code was found in server/src for this specific path family (grep for 'EPERM' returned no matches in server/src or tools/).

Not determined whether any deployment/process-management layer (outside this worktree, e.g. start.bat / tools/start-runtime.js) already prevents two BuilderGate processes from sharing one checkout's server/data/ directory at the same time; this worktree analysis is limited to server/src as instructed and does not include tools/start-runtime.js or start.bat behavior.
